notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Nikita Kucherov takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L2. Victor Hedman is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Lilleberg and Crozier.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Pontus Holmberg is out four weeks (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Yanni Gourde has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Ilya Mikheyev.
Erik Černák is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. Emil Lilleberg has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.
Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 7 games.
Kaiden Guhle is out (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-four defenseman.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games.
Mike Matheson is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman.
Dylan Larkin was added to the roster on Nov 24 and has played beside Alexandre Texier and Alex Newhook.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 25 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Lightning and the Canadiens go in level on 32 points, third and third in the Atlantic in the Atlantic. A win in regulation would put either one ahead of the other.

MTL.head: Close, but the Lightning have the slight edge
MTL.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Montréal has home-ice advantage, and the Lightning will be without Holmberg. The Canadiens’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

TBL.head: The Lightning have a slight edge
TBL.body: Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, but Montréal has home-ice advantage, and the Lightning will be without Holmberg. Still, it’s close: the Canadiens can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: A rematch of last spring’s first round
paras: Both teams come in on a three-game losing streak. Two good teams meet. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Lightning third (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Canadiens fourth (tied for ninth).

The Lightning’s record (.640) is about what their chances are worth. The Canadiens’ record (.615) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.541), largely because they’re 9-7 in one-goal games.

The Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), but don’t block many shots (29th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), and something has to give when the Canadiens’ shooting runs into their defense. On the other side, the Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). The Bolts have the edge over the Canadiens on preventing dangerous shots.

Nikita Kucherov (10 G / 23 A / 33 P in 25 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring, with eight goals in ten games against Montréal since 2023-24. Jake Guentzel (15 G / 16 A / 31 P in 25 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (5 G / 19 A / 24 P in 26 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 8 A / 20 P in 26 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.

Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-6-1 / .897 SV% in 18 GS) will likely start for Tampa Bay. Montréal has two options in net: Jacob Fowler (10-4-2 / .912 SV% in 16 GS) and Jakub Dobeš (4-4-2 / .868 SV% in 10 GS). Fowler has started seven of their last ten games, including the last one on Nov 25, so Montréal could turn to Dobeš to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

The Lightning are newly without Pontus Holmberg and Erik Černák.
The Canadiens are newly without Kaiden Guhle, and have been without Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Mike Matheson for several games.
